scope: Separate PR93-source warm serial arm diagnostic; not the new engine-only main source or a new-main performance result
controls: Fixed arm order AB/BA, identical originals/queries, existing arm protocol; no fs cache drop or cgroup isolation
limitations: Unique-token search is correctness/work diagnostic, not representative relevance or query mix
Short search/write series do not qualify tail percentiles or general throughput gains
Native local encryption differs from plaintext SQLite/JSONL; not matched confidentiality or hosted failure domains
Seed/reopen/full original verification included in each fresh store; clean reopen only, no new crash campaign

arm_info.name: native-record
arm_info.durability: native sealed Store sync=true; one durable append per <=1000 records; one host, no replication/backups
notes: actual native RecordLog and shared projection; current snapshot materialization, row validation/refresh, original reads and excerpts are inside each search
source IDs/known-at clocks and metadata persist as explicit benchmark import attributes; seconds convert to native microseconds; native assigned IDs/ingest clocks remain genuine and unchanged
native local Store compression/encryption differs from hosted per-object Zstd/S3/KMS; public fixture key, no hosted footprint/cost or failure-domain claim
RecordLog Store defaults: hot Zstd 3, dictionary cap 512KiB trained after 4MiB, hot-file target 64MiB, decode cache 4MiB; no explicit cold compaction in this arm

derived in-memory postings reuse requires a complete fresh view and identical retained rows; changes/removals rebuild; no disk index; native 100k-record/128MiB state bounds apply; >1000 input batches can recover partially before ACK

arm_info.name: sqlite-fts5
arm_info.durability: one transaction per batch; WAL + synchronous=FULL (fsync at commit)
notes: query = OR of distinct tokens; latest-revision filter in SQL

arm_info.name: jsonl-fts5
arm_info.version: Zstd 1.5.7; SQLite 3.53.2 contentless FTS5 porter unicode61 bm25
arm_info.durability: immutable batch file fsync + directory fsync, then SQLite WAL synchronous=FULL commit; one host, no replication/backups/encryption
notes: one JSONL frame per batch; no dictionary or deduplication; level 3 when compressed
same OR-token query/ranking and two-clock SQL visibility as sqlite arm; FTS5 stores no original text
all payloads, index, WAL/SHM and uncommitted orphan frames count toward footprint; no automatic orphan reclamation
get decodes each selected batch frame once per request; no retained payload cache
